question: Why does CI take 24 minutes on a typical pull request, and what would cut it most?
answer: Most of the time is the e2e suite running on one machine after the unit tests finish. Sharding it four ways and caching dependencies would bring a typical run to about 9 minutes; the other wins are small.

method.sample: 412 CI runs on main and pull requests
method.head: a8ef847
caveats: Time waiting in the queue isn't counted.

findings.title: Shard the e2e suite four ways
findings.change: Split Playwright into 4 shards with --shard and merge the reports.
findings.benefit: The e2e job drops from 14 to about 4 minutes.
findings.validate: Median CI time on main over a week.

findings.title: Cache dependencies between runs
findings.benefit: Install drops from 95 s to 8 s.

findings.title: Move tests to 8 vCPU runners
findings.change: Switch the test job to the 8-core larger runner, or keep 4 cores. I'd try it for a week.
findings.benefit: Perhaps 30% faster unit tests, at twice the price per minute.
findings.validate: A week of runs, and the bill.

minor.title: Drop the unused lint cache step
minor.change: Delete the cache step in lint.yml; it never hits.

notWorth.title: Self-hosted runners
notWorth.why: They save money only above about 40,000 minutes a month; we use 9,000.
